sentences.text: Nodosaurus was a herbivorous ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous, growing to roughly 4 to 6 meters long with bony dermal plates covering its body, possibly with spikes along its sides.
The unique variation in the arrangement of osteoderm rows on the posterior body is known to be exclusive to Nodosaurus.
A 2010 estimate by Paul suggests Nodosaurus reached a length of 6 meters and a weight of 3.5 tonnes.
The genus name means "knotted lizard" in Latin, referring to the bumps on the leg armor, while the species name means "braided," referring to the pattern of the armor.

Fossils of Nodosaurus were first discovered on July 17, 1881, by collector William Harlow Reed in Albany County, Wyoming, and Othniel Charles Marsh scientifically described the genus and named the species Nodosaurus textilis in 1889.

The genus is known from two incomplete fossil specimens that lack skulls, including the holotype, YPM 1815, found in the Belle Fourche Member of the Frontier Formation, which consists of a partial skeleton without a skull.

One of the known specimens was found in the Thermopolis Shale of Wyoming, while the holotype preserves three back vertebrae, thirteen tail vertebrae, a sacrum, ribs, parts of a scapula, humerus, left elbow and radius, metacarpals, phalanges, both ilia, a left femur, both tibiae, a left perone piece, a left foot, parts of the posterior dorsal armor, a left hip shield, a keeled osteoderm, a vertebral column, and a column-shaped plate.
No other findings have been assigned to the species except for some loose armor plates.
A third specimen is believed to exist in Mexico, but it has not been confirmed as Nodosaurus.
Nodosaurus likely ate soft plants due to its inability to chew tough fibrous ones, or it may have processed tough plants using gastroliths and a large intestinal apparatus.
Researchers suggest that without a tail club, Nodosaurus likely defended itself by rolling onto its back to expose only its armored sides and rear, similar to modern hedgehogs.
Nodosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia, with the family Nodosauridae and the type species Nodosaurus textilis.
Nodosaurus belongs to the subfamily Nodosaurinae within the family Nodosauridae.
Nodosaurus is the homonym of Nodosauridae, one of the two subgroups of Ankylosauria, and is found in this group in most studies.

Marsh originally placed Nodosaurus within Stegosauria in 1889, then named his own family Nodosauridae in 1890 but thought they were part of the Ceratopsia, before returning Nodosaurus to Stegosauria along with various other armored species in 1896.
Vickaryous et al. in 2004 found the findings too scarce for exact classification and listed them as "Ankylosauria incertae sedis."
In 1978, Walter Preston Coombs renamed taxa as Nodosaurus species, creating Nodosaurus sternbergi and Nodosaurus coleii.
The holotype dates to the middle Cenomanian, approximately 97 million years ago, while the time range for Nodosaurus is from the Cenomanian to the Maastrichtian (100.5 to 66 million years ago).
The dating of Nodosaurus has also been given as the Albian.
It is debated whether the nodosaurids Stegopelta and Hierosaurus are synonyms of Nodosaurus, a hypothesis proposed in 1978 that has received little support.
